evidence: getProject(projectId) does `this.repository.projects.get(projectId); if (!project) throw new Error(`Project ${projectId} not found`)`, the same lookup and check that addTask, assignTask, markTaskDone and listTasks each write out themselves.
addTask, assignTask, markTaskDone and listTasks don't call this.getProject(projectId) even though it exists, so they bypass the module's own abstraction.
assignTask and markTaskDone both repeat `project.tasks.find((t) => t.id === taskId); if (!task) throw new Error(`Task ${taskId} not found`)`.
createUser(userId, name) sits in TaskService alongside the task and project operations. This is a minor mixing of concerns, and it is justified because assignTask checks that the user exists.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
src/application/taskService.ts is the only file in the module, and it has one clear concern: managing projects, users and tasks through an injected Repository. It fails the rubric on duplication and bypass, not on a split of concerns.

The "project must exist" check is a lookup, a not-found test and the same Error message. It is written out separately in addTask, assignTask, markTaskDone, listTasks and getProject. The class already has getProject(projectId), which does exactly this lookup and check. The other four methods don't call it and copy its body instead, so they bypass the module's own abstraction. The "task must exist in project" check is also copied in assignTask and markTaskDone. If one of these invariants changes, it has to be changed in several places.

createUser is a small extra concern (managing users) inside a class focused on tasks. assignTask needs users, so this is minor.

violations.message: The project-existence check (repository.projects.get plus `Project ${projectId} not found`) is repeated in addTask, assignTask, markTaskDone, listTasks and getProject. The other methods should call the existing getProject() so the rule lives in one place.
The task-existence check (`project.tasks.find` plus `Task ${taskId} not found`) is repeated in assignTask and markTaskDone. It should be a single shared lookup.
